name: bm-e1-actomyosin-cortex
title: E1 — Explicit LAMMPS actomyosin cortex
question: Can a coarse explicit actomyosin filament/crosslink/motor model reproduce the cortical tension, strain response and relaxation that an effective Tyssue cortical-energy term represents?
hypothesis: A 2D cell-sized coarse filament/crosslink/motor LAMMPS patch produces a tunable active tension and a strain response/relaxation that map onto Tyssue cortical-energy parameters, so the effective cortical term can be replaced by explicit actin without changing the measured confinement in the overlap regime.
objective: Build a coarse filament/crosslink/motor LAMMPS model on a 2D cell-sized patch; measure tension, strain response and relaxation; map these onto Tyssue cortical-energy parameters. NEW extension - the paper does not explicitly simulate actin.
description:
First mechanistic extension beyond the paper (plan section 5). A coarse actomyosin cortex
(filaments, crosslinks, motors) is built as a LAMMPS patch and characterised (tension,
strain response, relaxation), then mapped to the effective Tyssue cortical-energy
parameters. This is explicitly a NEW extension, not a reproduction target; its fidelity
decision (reduced cortical model vs molecularly-resolved actin) is an open decision in the
plan. Care is taken not to double-count tension when the effective cortical term is replaced
by explicit actin.

expected_behavior.name: actin-maps-to-cortical-energy
expected_behavior.observable: cortical tension / strain response / relaxation of the patch
expected_behavior.rationale: The explicit cortex must reproduce the effective cortical-energy behaviour in an overlap regime before it can replace the Tyssue term (P4).

baseline.name: bm-e1-actomyosin-cortex
baseline.note: Implemented over the viva-lammps model seam (LammpsModelProcess + the actomyosin-cortex plugin): resolves ready and runs in real LAMMPS; the contractility knob tunes cortical tension. v0 coarse cortex — not yet filament-resolved; mapping to a Tyssue cortical-energy parameter is the next step (E2).
